rows.sourceSentence: Firm limits need not mean turning the home into a battlefield.

blockers.finding: Both wrong choices are implausible absolutes (“schedule proves the siblings never disagreed”; “clear rule requires everyone to argue every night”). The learner can reject them without applying the source metaphor or the shared-desk facts.
blockers.repair: Replace with context-compatible near misses that preserve at least part of the scheduling story but misstate the effect or scope; keep exactly one best target answer.

advisories.finding: “It made the family stop speaking to one another” is another remote foil; a plausible misunderstanding of the rule/weekly review would test comprehension better.

rows.sourceSentence: Their new office is gadget-heavy but easy to use.

blockers.finding: The scene lists smart curtains, tablet controls and voice assistant, so “contains no electronic features” is impossible without reading the expression; together with option c’s blanket “must be easy” claim, the two foils offer no plausible interpretation of a gadget-rich but hard-to-learn room.
blockers.repair: Use at least one context-compatible near miss (for example, correctly note the devices but wrongly claim the half-hour learning period proves ease or physical weight); preserve one uniquely best answer and bilingual alignment.

advisories.finding: “It has no electronic equipment at all” is an obvious contradiction to the enumerated devices; a more credible device/usability mix would provide stronger discrimination.
Chinese “展覽設備雖然繁多” omits the electronic-device sense conveyed by gadget-heavy; adding 電子 would make the bilingual target explicit.
